notes: could not is split under rule 35's two-word clause — not to לֹא, could to the verb — since no יָכֹל stands in the Hebrew and nothing is indivisible.
The fourth clause writes like unto, which settles the split between דָּמָה and אֶל and supports leaving s011 unrepresented in the second clause; the competing reading there is named.
nor (t029) rests on the present לֹא alone: כָּל־עֵץ opens with no waw in the projection (rule 35).
fir trees and plane trees are headed on fir and plane by rule 31's subtraction, as palm trees heads on palm.
